questions.q: How did James help the horses on long uphill roads?
choices: He set the wheels a little across the road to give them a breathing
He made them trot faster so they would reach the top of the hill sooner
He got down from the box and pushed the carriage from behind
He stopped and took off their harness so they could rest
questions.evidence: he set the carriage wheels a little across the road

questions.q: What did the head hostler at the hotel look like?
choices: A pleasant little man with a crooked leg and a yellow striped waistcoat
A tall, broad man with a thick black beard and a very loud and gruff voice
A young stable boy with a pipe always stuck in his mouth
A thin, bent old man who walked slowly with a stick
questions.evidence: with a crooked leg, and a yellow striped waistcoat

questions.q: What surprised James about the way the old hostler cleaned Black Beauty?
choices: He was quick and thorough at the same time
He washed him all over with icy cold water
He talked to the horse the whole time in French
He never touched the feet or the mane at all
questions.evidence: you do beat all I ever saw for being quick and thorough at the same time

questions.q: The hostler said "practice makes perfect." What did he mean?
choices: Doing something many times makes you good at it
It is better not to practice too much at anything
Only perfect people can do a job without practice
Practice is something only children need to do

questions.q: How did the hostler's job as a jockey come to an end?
choices: His horse Larkspur fell at Goodwood and he broke his knee
He grew too tall and too heavy to ride in the races any more
He was sent away for being too slow on the course
He grew tired of racing and asked to work in a stable
questions.evidence: my poor Larkspur got a fall, and I broke my knee

questions.q: What did the hostler say he could tell after handling a horse for twenty minutes?
choices: What sort of groom the horse has had
Exactly how old the horse is in years
How fast the horse can run a mile
What the horse likes best to eat
questions.evidence: I'll tell you what sort of a groom he has had

questions.q: What did the hostler say about the leap where young Gordon was killed?
choices: It was a bad place, where a horse had no chance to see where it was going
It was an easy jump that any good hunter could take without trouble
The horse was to blame because it had refused the same jump before
The fence there was too low to stop a horse from jumping it
questions.evidence: No chance for a horse to see where he is going

questions.q: What is the old hostler's main lesson about horses?
choices: Their tempers are made by how they are treated when young
Horses should always be cleaned slowly and very gently
Only racehorses ever have good manners in the stable
Horses soon forget how they were treated as foals
questions.evidence: their tempers are mostly made when they are young
